e: Abundant means existing in large quantities, i.e. plentiful.
Candid means open and honest in speech, i.e. frank.
Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, i.e. painstaking.
Obsequious means excessively eager to please or obey, i.e. servile.
Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time.
Ancient means very old; its opposite is modern.
Generous means giving freely; stingy means unwilling to give.
An optimist expects good outcomes; a pessimist expects the worst.
Transparent lets light pass through; opaque does not.
Affluent means wealthy; impoverished means very poor.
Garrulous means excessively talkative; taciturn means habitually silent.
Diligent means hardworking and careful; its opposite is lazy.

q: One-word substitute: A person who does not believe in the existence of God.
e: An atheist denies God's existence; an agnostic holds that it cannot be known.

q: One-word substitute: A person who can speak two languages.
e: Bilingual means able to speak two languages; a polyglot knows many.

q: One-word substitute: A place where birds are kept.
e: An aviary houses birds; an apiary is for bees.

q: One-word substitute: Government by the people, through elected representatives.
e: Democracy is rule by the people, usually through elected representatives.

q: One-word substitute: A speech made without any preparation.
e: An extempore speech is delivered without preparation.

q: One-word substitute: An abnormal fear of heights.
e: Acrophobia is the fear of heights; claustrophobia is the fear of closed spaces.

q: One-word substitute: One who walks in sleep.
e: A somnambulist is a sleepwalker; an insomniac cannot sleep.

q: One-word substitute: A person who does not eat meat, fish or eggs.
e: A vegetarian avoids meat and lives on plant-based food.

q: What does the idiom 'a piece of cake' mean?
e: 'A piece of cake' describes a task that is very easy to do.

q: What does the idiom 'to bury the hatchet' mean?
e: To bury the hatchet is to end a quarrel and become friendly again.

q: What does the idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' mean?
o: To work or study late into the night
e: It means to stay up late working or studying.

q: What does the idiom 'once in a blue moon' mean?
e: 'Once in a blue moon' means something that happens very seldom.

q: What does the idiom 'to beat about the bush' mean?
o: To avoid coming to the main point
To work hard in the fields
e: To beat about the bush is to talk around a subject without getting to the point.

q: What does the idiom 'a white elephant' mean?
o: A possession that is costly to maintain but of little use
e: A white elephant is something expensive to keep whose usefulness does not justify the cost.
